atoms.b: Although most people think of volcanoes as tall peaks in the sky, the majority are actually hidden on the ((forest ++sea)) floor. Underwater volcanoes are known as submarine volcanoes.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: When a volcano erupts under the sea, superheated water is created, which is liquid water with a temperature of over 100 °C. This is only made possible by the high pressure found deep underwater.

Eruptions also cause cracks, called fissures, to form in the Earth’s surface. Minerals come out of these cracks and crystallise around the fissure to create a chimney-like structure called a black smoker.

a type of volcano named after the black smoke that escapes from its crater

hint.label: Did you know?
hint.text: Unlike most life on Earth, these creatures do not need any sunlight to live!

feedback.finish: These creatures feed on the bacteria that survive around black smokers.

instruction.text: Select the island to find out more.

feedback.finish: Volcanic islands are formed by underwater volcanoes. Lava solidifies, turns into rock and slowly builds up over time until it breaks through the ocean’s surface.

hint.text: Submarine volcanoes exist all over the world — many at thousands of metres below sea level!

atoms.a: Scientists are finished researching underwater volcanoes.
